title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono attend custody hearing in St Thomas | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono attended a custody hearing for Ono’s seven-year-old daughter Kyoko on 27 July 1971.

The two-hour hearing took place on the island of St Thomas, before Judge Almeric Christian. Lennon and Ono were represented by Campbell, Loud and Dennenberg, and Ono’s former husband Tony Cox was represented by Bailey, Wood and Rosenberg.

Cox’s lawyers alleged that the court had no sway in the case because he and Kyoko were currently resident in Texas. Ono’s lawyers countered that since Cox changed location frequently, and because he had filed a divorce order in the locality, any St Thomas ruling should be upheld.

During a recess, Ono was served with a summons for a custody hearing in Houston, Texas.

She later took the stand, testifying that she and Lennon had spent more than £50,000 in child support and travel expenses. She told the court that Cox rarely informed her of Kyoko’s locations, and that she did not want full custody.

Ono also alleged that Kyoko, whom Cox had renamed Kay, had fallen behind in her schooling, and that Ono was concerned about his temper and possessiveness.

Lennon then took the stand, telling the court that he would be “simply thrilled” to have Kyoko in his family. “In fact,” he said, “since she is the same age as my son, I would love to see them get married. She is a sweet child.”

The judge decreed that St Thomas did hold jurisdiction over the custody of Kyoko, and rejected Cox’s lawyers’ claim that the court should defer to Texas rulings.

On Friday 30 July, the District Court in the Virgin Islands directed Cox to appear in St Thomas on 16 September to demonstrate why custody should not be awarded to Ono. The order was sent to Bailey, Wood and Rosenberg, as well as his Houston lawyers Sewell, Junell and Riggs.
